glosses: To produce offspring sexually; to bear young.

examples.text: Plant breeding is always a numbers game.[…]The wild species we use are rich in genetic variation, and individual plants are highly heterozygous and do not breed true. In addition, we are looking for rare alleles, so the more plants we try, the better.

glosses: To give birth to; to be the native place of.

examples.text: A pond breeds fish.

glosses: To mate.

To arrange the mating of (specific animals).

examples.text: She wanted to breed her cow to the neighbor's registered bull.

glosses: To propagate or grow (plants) in an effort to give (them) certain qualities.

examples.text: He tries to breed blue roses.

glosses: To take care of in infancy and through childhood; to bring up.

glosses: To be formed in the parent or dam; to be generated or to grow, like young before birth.
